title: Step 67-E permission/scope-aware Admin shell and safe destination navigation
description: MEDIUM-risk Admin frontend shell authorization-context stage. Read server-authoritative permissions/scopes for the authenticated staff session, fail closed on invalid/revoked context, expose only repository-proven destination handoffs whose unblocked gap-free runtime operations have permission alternatives fully satisfied by the current permission set, present server-assigned scopes without editing RBAC, provide neutral deep-link denial, breadcrumb and local destination-title search. Destination visibility never authorizes operations; later domain workspaces remain unimplemented.

dependencies.evidence: PR #355 merged; exact-SHA Canonical CI #1797, Phase A #1296 and CodeQL #943 SUCCESS; terminal Lock release comment 6145858971.

evidence.operation_authority: BACKEND_ONLY; destination visibility is never an operation authorization grant
evidence.destination_source: Step56 final audit operation/surface matrices + Admin shell destination labels/groups
evidence.destination_transport: generic Step67 shell handoff by design surface id; not a later-domain runtime URL

acceptance_criteria.description: Authenticated shell reads /admin/me/permissions and /admin/me/scopes server-side using the existing Admin cookie bridge; browser credential/token storage remains absent.
Permission and scope payloads are validated, normalized and deduplicated; malformed or unsupported context fails closed without protected navigation.

Destination registry is generated only from repository-proven Step56 operation/surface evidence. Unblocked, gap-free runtime operations contribute permission alternatives; unresolved or blocked operations never grant visibility.
A destination is visible only when at least one eligible operation alternative has all its required runtime permissions satisfied. Surface permission union is never used as an authorization shortcut.
Server-assigned scopes are presented as immutable context only. No scope mutation, impersonation or invented scope-to-destination mapping is introduced.
Generic design-surface handoff routes re-check current permission context server-side. Unknown and unauthorized deep links render the same neutral denial without entity/count/PII/secret leakage.
Breadcrumb uses only shell group label + permitted destination label and no domain entity data.
Local search searches only currently permitted destination labels/surface references; no customer/order/product/entity lookup or backend search is issued.
Quick navigation only opens the authorized generic handoff review surface; no command, mutation or later-domain workspace is executed.
Session/permission/scope revocation is observed on server loader revalidation and stale sensitive destination state is not cached.
No Step-Up UX, dashboard metric runtime, Backend/OpenAPI/database/Storefront/Product-Design/Current-State mutation or Steps 68-73 domain workspace is introduced.

MEDIUM-risk closure requires exact-head Canonical CI, Phase A, CodeQL/deterministic Review, exact-artifact ACTIVE Lock, protected merge, exact-SHA postmerge verification and terminal Lock release. Human Gate is not required.

external_gate_evidence.rule: Step 67-E is MEDIUM risk and does not require Project Owner Human Gate.
